Capability.meaning: Explicit operation grant on a resource or permission scope.

PrincipalGroup.meaning: Direct membership in a configured role or user group; a group can itself be a member. Supplied by trusted configuration or an authoritative identity source, never inferred from an agent-chosen name.

ResourceGroup.meaning: Permission-scope membership; grants on a parent apply to its descendants.

InGroup.meaning: Direct or nested role/user-group membership from PrincipalGroup. Membership alone is not permission.

Can.meaning: Grant including declared principal and resource memberships; not final authorization.

Field.meaning: Host-observed field or association of an application object or event. The binding defines cardinality, value type, fixed unit and optional observation-time field; never agent claims or hidden policy decisions.

Event.meaning: An event observed by the host, with its ID, actor and kind; recording it does not imply permission or success.

scope: Captured gate inputs and mediated callbacks. Outcomes follow the trusted adapter's confirmation contract; they are not independent proof of business success or authentic identity. Unmediated channels and missing observations remain outside this trace.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Add the four with one line each on what they take (assistant layer, search default, advertising dollars, the post-phone form factor), what they would need to take more, and the signpost that would show entry. Microsoft and OpenAI matter because the thesis says the AI layer is rented; Meta because glasses could move the upgrade cycle off the phone.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Four named threats are absent from the competitor table. Microsoft (Windows and Copilot, Surface, Bing as the search-default counterfactual, the only peer near Apple's multiple) appears only in valuation ratios. OpenAI is the substitute Siri was rebuilt to match, is named with Apple in the xAI suit the risk section cites, and is the plausible source of a per-query licence. Amazon (Alexa+, Fire, AWS and Trainium, ads inside the $1.34T pool) and Meta (Ray-Ban glasses; the destination for Apple's departed AI researchers) are missing. Status quo and Spotify are included, so the gap is selective, not structural.","sections":["competition","technology_product","market"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Add as rows or state why they are outside the frame.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Transsion and Motorola appear only in the market section's regional table, and Epic or alternative marketplaces only as a legal effect rather than a competitor with a take rate.","sections":["competition"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Candidates tested and found adequately covered: Samsung (unit scale, mobile loss), Huawei (China premium, HarmonyOS), Xiaomi (margin structure), Google (Gemini supply and Pixel), Lenovo/HP/Dell (PC share), Spotify (music), Alphabet (advertising), plus status quo and device longevity. Suppliers excluded correctly as non-rivals: Qualcomm and TSMC (insourced modem, 2nm allocation), Nvidia (compute not sold to consumers). Open source has no direct analogue to iOS, but OpenHarmony and AOSP forks deserve one line as the commoditisation path in emerging markets. Academic spin-outs are not a credible threat to a scaled platform; the nearest equivalent is model labs, covered by the OpenAI item.

Where Apple discloses no units, label the decomposition an inference.","evidence_request":"Replacement-cycle and installed-base estimates by region; US carrier promotions and upgrade rates around the 2026-09-18 iPhone 18 launch.","issue":"The 22% iPhone growth is never decomposed into units, price and mix, and the only launch evidence for the $100 price rise is three weeks of China sell-through (+23.5%). IDC has units down 16.7% and value up 6.3%, so growth is price-led by construction, but whether the $1,199 Pro holds volume in the US, where carrier financing and upgrade rates set demand, is unanswered. The hardest sell - persuading an installed base to replace at a higher price into a second year of memory inflation - is described, not evidenced.","sections":["market","competition","business_model"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Name the one datapoint that would settle it (Pro-mix or attach rate after 2026-09-18) and label the AI upgrade premise unverified until then.","evidence_request":"","issue":"No price or revenue evidence ties Siri AI to an upgrade: the $100 increase is attributed to memory cost, and the assistant ships as an English beta. The strategy section concedes the AI spend may be 'a cost of staying in the conversation', which leaves the AI premise of the upgrade cycle with no demand-side support in the report.","sections":["technology_product","strategy"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: PMF questions and how the report stands: budget owner - answered (consumer or carrier plan for hardware; developer and subscriber for commissions). Sales cycle - answered (September launch, carrier channel, annual cadence). Why adoption is not faster - answered (Siri 23 months late, English beta, rented model, no AI revenue line). Lost deals - not addressed; Apple discloses none, so it should be stated as a gap. Hardest thing about selling - described but not evidenced. The China pull-forward and the spring-2027 split launch are the two real risks to the demand read, and both are already flagged.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Recompute (a) on one basis, trailing to trailing and forward to forward, and reconcile (b): state which constraint sets the 0.75-1.0% first tranche when the Kelly fraction is 3.9% and the cap 5%.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Two mechanics fail. (a) 'the trailing multiple is 10.8% above Apple's own twelve-month average of 35.66 times' compares a trailing P/E of 39.5x with a forward average. (b) 'the odds support a fractional Kelly well above the cap, so the cap binds' against a full Kelly of 39% and a one-tenth fraction of 3.9%, with a 5% cap and a 0.75-1.0% first tranche: 3.9% is below the cap, so the cap does not bind, and the tranche is a quarter of the fraction computed.","sections":["scoring"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Label it a spread check on current free cash flow and show the DCF's 4.0% terminal growth beside it.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The '6.4-6.9% perpetual growth' is a Gordon spread check on current free cash flow ($125.1bn / (9.0%-6.5%) = about $5.0tn), not the DCF, whose terminal growth is 4.0% and which produces $212. Both can be true, but the reader is left to reconcile a 6.5% perpetuity with a $212 DCF.","sections":["funding_valuation","executive_summary"],"severity":"Minor"},{"action":"State the span each growth rate refers to.","evidence_request":"","issue":"'Revenue compounded at 5.0% a year from FY2021' is FY2021-to-TTM; FY2021-FY2025 is 3.3%, as the market and scoring sections correctly say. The valuation line reads as if 5.0% covered the filed years.","sections":["funding_valuation"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Thirty-percent-worse stress test, run on the report's own inputs. Margin 30% worse (47-48% to about 45.2%): EPS -7% to $9.10, $264 at 29x, so the $270 entry sits inside the softened base rather than below it. Multiple 30% worse: 35.2x to 24.6x = $241, exactly the stated bear. Services growth 30% worse (12-14% to 8.4-9.8%): services EBIT $62.7bn at 23x loses about $29 a share, taking the parts to $148. Payment 30% larger ($26bn): a ban costs 16% of EPS, not 12.9%. Revenue 30% lower: operating income $94.6bn and EPS $5.3, which ties to the risk section. The 'do not own at $344.63' call strengthens on every path; the $270 entry survives only the margin case, which the thesis already concedes.
